title: Kyoto vs Nara: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Kyoto for multi-day stays, temples, and food. Nara for the deer, Todai-ji, and a peaceful day trip. Do both — they're 45 minutes apart.

categories.name: Temples & Cultural Highlights
categories.summary: Kyoto has 2,000+ temples and 17 UNESCO sites. Nara's Todai-ji and Kasuga Taisha are world-class but coverable in one day.

categories.name: The Deer Park
categories.summary: Nara's 1,200 free-roaming sika deer are uniquely unforgettable. Nothing in Kyoto compares.

categories.name: Food & Dining
categories.summary: Kyoto has kaiseki, matcha culture, Nishiki Market, and serious izakayas. Nara's food is tourist-oriented near the park.

categories.name: Cost
categories.summary: Nara is 20-30% cheaper on accommodation. Deer park entry is free; only Todai-ji charges (¥800).

categories.name: Getting Around
categories.summary: Nara's walkable layout beats Kyoto's bus-dependent transit for ease within the city.

categories.name: Nightlife & Evening Options
categories.summary: Gion and Pontocho offer atmospheric evening walks and dining. Nara largely shuts down by 9pm.

categories.name: Family-Friendliness
categories.summary: The deer park is a hit for all ages. Open green spaces are easier with strollers than Kyoto's temple paths.

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: Kyoto is the better regional hub — Osaka, Hiroshima, Himeji, Uji, and Nara all within easy reach.

faq.question: Should I visit Kyoto or Nara on a Japan trip?
faq.answer: Most travelers should do Kyoto as the base and Nara as a day trip — they're only 45 minutes apart by Kintetsu Limited Express. Kyoto offers far more depth; Nara is a perfect day trip for the deer park, Todai-ji, and a slower pace.

faq.question: How far apart are Kyoto and Nara?
faq.answer: 35 km by road, 45 minutes by Kintetsu Limited Express (¥1,160). JR Nara Line takes 50–75 minutes for ¥720.

faq.question: Which is cheaper — Kyoto or Nara?
faq.answer: Nara is noticeably cheaper — accommodation is 20–30% less, and the deer park is free. Only Todai-ji (¥800) charges significant entry.
